2.question: Why don't I see Nibbana right now?

screen_verbatim: Due to the very ignorance of the fact that it is seeing because it is looking, the dog imagines another dog, there, in the water. What is called maññanā is an imagining of that sort.
Only a looking is there, nothing worth looking at. Only a seeing is there, nothing to be seen. Apart from the bare act of hearing, there is nothing to be heard.
There is no seer, apart from the phenomenon of seeing, according to the Tathāgata... For the worldling, the bare act of seeing carries with it a perception of 'one who sees'.
pointer.screen_plain: You do not see Nirvana right now because in the act of your seeing you imagine a world. There is no seer apart from seeing: only looking, nothing worth looking at; only seeing, nothing to be seen.
